contexts.evidence: Introduction and §4, Fig. 4: several modified backward rules retain maps after parameter randomization, supporting the reliability concern.
§§2–4 analyze loss of later-layer information and class insensitivity in several modified backward rules.
§2 treats z+, alpha-beta, and z rules. It diagnoses rank-one convergence, not epsilon attenuation; the conservative z rule is explicitly nonconvergent.
contexts.proposed_replacement: The retained map structure is consistent with parameter-insensitivity concerns for some relevance-propagation rules~\parencite{sixt2020whenexplanationslie}, but this comparison does not identify the mechanism in SplitLRP.

contexts.evidence: §4, Fig. 4(b), reports retained saliency structure under cascading parameter randomization; thesis-specific architectures and numerical results are separate.
Introduction and §5 connect insensitivity to later-layer parameters with failure to explain model predictions faithfully; routing-law claims are thesis results.
§4, Fig. 4, demonstrates similar attribution maps after randomization. The trajectory theorem itself is not attributed to Sixt.

notes: No publication DOI is supplied by PMLR. The paper does not establish that conservation alone causes parameter insensitivity.

verified_metadata.title: Monotonic Networks
verified_metadata.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 10 (NIPS 1997)

metadata_sources.supports: Official title, author, proceedings volume and conference year.
Publisher MIT Press and official download URL.

contexts.evidence: §2, pp. 662–664: sign-constrained affine functions composed with monotone minimum/maximum operations guarantee coordinatewise monotonicity.
§§1–2 provide an early sign-constrained monotone architecture, supporting the historical lineage; the interpretable-core description is the thesis framing.
§1, p. 662, cites earlier monotonicity work and an adaptive logic network. This paper does not establish the unrestricted historical priority claim oldest.
contexts.proposed_replacement: Weight-sign constraints are a longstanding device for building monotone models \parencite{Sill1997_MonotonicNetworks,Daniels2010_MonotoneNN} and remain the structural core of modern certified-monotone architectures \parencite{Liu2020CertifiedMonotone,Runje_2023}.

contexts.evidence: §2 restricts functions to the chosen monotonicity class. §3 proves universal approximation within that class, so the expressivity statement holds relative to unconstrained functions.

notes: Existing PDF URL under /hash/ returns HTTP 404; the correct official PDF path uses /file/.
The universal approximation theorem is within the monotone target class; do not read the expressivity citation as proving an approximation deficit inside that class.

metadata_sources.supports: Exact title, complete ordered authors and ICLR 2024 status.

artifact.version_note: Official ICLR 2024 proceedings PDF; first-page authors and conference header verified.

contexts.evidence: §2 identifies high-norm feature-map artifacts; §§2.2–3 add register tokens and evaluate their removal, supporting artifact-aware constructions.
§§2.1–2.2 concern high-norm background tokens repurposed for global information. They do not establish a connection to periodic grid artifacts from 16×16 tokenization.
contexts.proposed_replacement: On the vision side, DAVE \parencite{Wrobel2024} traced grid artifacts to the $16{\times}16$ patch tokenization of \acp{vit} \parencite{Dosovitskiy2021vit} and countered them with \emph{conditioned} (detached) operators and attribution averaging over random spatial transformations. Separately, \textcite{darcet2024vision} identified high-norm artifact tokens in feature maps and mitigated them with register tokens.

notes: Only the Darcet-related clause was audited; the accuracy of the DAVE attribution is covered by its own reference audit.

verified_metadata.title: Advancing Attribution-Based Neural Network Explainability through Relative Absolute Magnitude Layer-Wise Relevance Propagation and Multi-Component Evaluation
verified_metadata.venue: ACM Transactions on Intelligent Systems and Technology 15(3), pp. 1–30

metadata_sources.supports: Author-submitted manuscript identifies exact title, ordered authors, ACM TIST 15(3), 2024, pages 1–30 and published DOI.
Publisher-deposited DOI record corroborates ordered authors, volume 15 issue 3, pages 1–30, online publication 15 April 2024 and issue publication 30 June 2024.

artifact.version_note: Author accepted manuscript deposited as arXiv:2412.09311v1 in December 2024; first page identifies published DOI and April 2024 date. Template header says volume 1 issue 1, but arXiv journal reference and publisher-deposited record correctly give 15(3).

contexts.evidence: §3.1, pp. 8–10, introduces absLRP using positive contributions divided by absolute net output, and contrastive signed initialization across output classes. This supports the grouped statement about redistribution variants.

§3.1, pp. 8–10, develops an independent magnitude-normalized LRP rule for CNNs and ViTs, including detached normalizers. It is not presented as an AttnLRP extension, and the paper neither cites AttnLRP nor studies LLMs.
contexts.proposed_replacement: AttnLRP \parencite{Achtibat2024AttnLRP} systematized this into dedicated rules for the bilinear products and non-linearities, scaling to \acp{llm}. Related LRP variants include concept-level CRP \parencite{Achtibat2023CRP} and magnitude-aware absLRP \parencite{vukadin2024abslrp}.

notes: Bibliography metadata matches the published article. ACM landing page returned HTTP 403; publisher-deposited DOI metadata and the authors’ explicit publication reference supply venue verification.
Sign-aware is imprecise for absLRP: its distinguishing rule uses absolute net-output normalization; output initialization supplies signed contrast.
